\begin{CRchronicle}{106}
On the tenth day of the deep-winter month the district’s arithmetic changed for the tenth time where two hundred people stood. Berr Clay came up short off the clay road with the red cord of his office folded under his coat and, under the hot clay of him, the smell of nothing at all. He wiped his thumb twice, passed a finger over the figure through his sleeve, and read one in twelve twice over the basket --- once for the moot, once for the late households --- denying the levy with \emph{your house}, never \emph{I}. The block answered nothing; he went off with the box locked and Stone’s first true subtraction inside beside the nine, believing he had done a kindness. Hessa Rale took the slate up toward Greybank before noon with the writing to her sleeve, answering that she carried it and did not read it. The bell went four, four and a gap, and nobody crossed himself.

The boy in the basket kept the count nobody under any roof kept: three hundred and sixty-nine days, then three hundred and seventy, then three hundred and seventy-one, six months and one hundred and ninety-one days told by nobody. Ten readings stood behind one unsigned figure and ten were not one account; the figure read was still not the figure paid, and no doctrine came out of ten. On the eleventh morning Ilva drew at the well and answered what Stone’s firings had taken with \emph{Ask the pot what it cost. I keep the count, not the account}, her hand to her sleeve before her eyes to the asker and the strip of birch unread.

On the twelfth morning Sella Vail carried him two doors down to the Drawing house and set the basket at the edge of the light, where he could see and not join. The collector, cuff soft from washing and fingertips grey as skimmed milk gone off, set a cold iron tube against the neighbour’s forearm by touch without pressing. The neighbour gave under it with a small flat knock and was left with a pale round place, not a wound and no blood. On the other side a rekindled child went worse on the third day, grey at the fingertips and red at the hairline, while the room called it a graft settling and the mother held a cup of warm milk she never drank. The surgeon knew that pink returning to a face is the surface still cold and not the core; he could not speak, reach or warm. Under the Vail roof the house kept four pulls and the silence where the fifth should have stood. She carried him home and said nothing of where they had been, and the hand outside the wool came down on the three hundred and eighteenth answer, laid where the next hand would find it without looking.
\end{CRchronicle}
